newsitem.title: INDIA: India L&T 6-mth orders booked up 21 pct.
newsitem.headline: India L&T 6-mth orders booked up 21 pct.

text.p: Indian engineering and construction firm Larsen & Toubro Ltd said it booked orders worth 31.03 billion rupees in the first six months of 1996/97 (April-March), up 21 percent compared to year-ago period.

"Although the order booking for the first six months was very good, resulting in a healthy order backlog for the company, there are signs of delays in finalising new contracts," the company said in a statement.
"One of the main reasons for this slowing down is paucity of long-term funds for executing projects," it said.
"Some of the customers are also facing difficulties in arranging short-term funds for operations," it said.
It said the cement industry showed a very healthy growth of about 11 percent in the first six months of the current year.
"The prices also were ruling at reasonable levels till middle of September 1996," it said.
"However, in the last two months, the industry witnessed slackness in the demand resulting in pressure on prices."
"Moreover, there was an unprecedented increase in manufacturing costs due to increase in oil prices, railway freight, coal prices and power tariff by most states," it said.

L&T said its new cement plant in Gujarat started commercial production in the first half. The work on the second phase was progressing satisfactorily and due to be commissioned in the last quarter of the current fiscal year.
The Tadapatri cement plant in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh is expected to be commissioned in the next fiscal.
The glass container project in Nashik in western India has also started commercial production.
